summary: Discovery for Nebula Metrics evaluating Redwood self-serve API with discussion of hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer wants fastest time-to-first-token for a lightweight PLG onramp, but has enterprise security and data residency constraints for certain workloads. Agreed to pilot hosted with credits for initial TTFT and a subsequent technical deep dive for latency/cost benchmarks on dedicated/private if needed.
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-07 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood), Leah (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood), Ravi (CTO), Maya (Product), Jon (Backend), Elena (Infra)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. quick intro round, maybe 30s each?
[00:18] Ravi (Customer): Hi, Ravi Narang, CTO at Nebula Metrics. We do telemetry-driven analytics for SaaS apps, looking to add llm-powered insights into dashboards.
[00:30] Maya: Maya, product, focused on UX flows for automated insights.
[00:38] Jon: Jon, backend eng, I'll be integrating the API.
[00:44] Elena: Elena, infra, mostly concerned about data residency and our VPC requirements.
[00:50] Samir: Great. Quick agenda — understanding current stack/timeline, TTFT for a PLG onramp, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security requirements, and next steps. Anything to add?
[01:05] Maya: No, that sounds good. We're pretty time sensitive; want to show a working demo to leadership in 3 weeks.
[01:12] Samir: Perfect, should be doable. Couple quick qualifiers: what does your current infra look like? cloud vendor, anything on-prem?
[01:22] Jon: We're on AWS with VPCs, using k8s for most services. No on-prem yet but some regulated customers require EU-only data residency.
[01:34] Samir: Good context. Our PLG path is usually self-serve API — you sign up, we issue credits, and you can be to first token within hours. For production we offer Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
[01:52] Elena: When you say "first token within hours" — is there anything custom we need to run? network peering, infra setup?
[02:01] Leah (SE): For the hosted quickstart, minimal. We provision a trial project, assign credits, and you call our REST/SDK endpoints. No peering required. If you want VPC/private, that's a longer onboarding (we do a control-plane conn and can offer an on-prem package) — usually weeks depending on legal.
[02:20] Ravi: Ok — main success criteria for us: 1) quick demo to leadership, 2) measurable latency under 250ms P95 for our default prompts, 3) clear cost per inference so PM can plan.
[02:33] Samir: Nice and specific. For P95 under 250ms — for hosted we have curated model profiles; smaller open models can meet that depending on sequence length. For guaranteed SLA we'd look at Dedicated with reserved GPUs.
[02:49] Maya: Can you give a rough of cost difference between hosted vs dedicated?
[02:55] Samir: Ballpark: hosted is usage-based — per-token + per-embedding; it's great for early experiments. Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit that amortizes lower per-token cost at scale but has a higher fixed monthly. We'll send a tiered spreadsheet.
[03:12] Jon: How about caching / batching? We have bursty QPS and some interactive flows.
[03:20] Leah: We support automatic batching and KV caching. Note, KV cache sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in some docs, but it's cache. Caching helps conversational flows and reduces token cost without hurting latency in most cases.
[03:35] Elena: Security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. Also EU data residency.
[03:46] Samir: We are SOC2 Type II, support SAML/SSO and RBAC. For encryption at rest we integrate with KMS/HSM. Audit logs and retention windows are configurable on Dedicated/Private; some of these are limited on hosted but we do offer enterprise features for compliance. We'll attach our security whitepaper.
[04:05] Ravi: If we go hosted for pilot, how do you handle data retention and purge?
[04:12] Leah: Hosted has configurable retention; for sensitive tenants we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control retention and egress.
[04:22] Maya: For the demo we want the fastest time-to-first-token. What's the typical onramp flow?
[04:28] Samir: Sign up, create API key, we issue credits (we usually give a promo credit pack for POCs), you run a few calls, and you can embed in front end. We also provide sample prompts and an eval harness. Time-to-first-token is sometimes under an hour if you don't need VPC peering.
[04:45] Jon: Are there SDKs? Node/Python?
[04:49] Leah: Yes — official SDKs in Python, Node, and examples for Java.
[04:53] Jon: Great. On the latency front, can we run a benchmark?
[04:57] Leah: Absolutely. For that we typically run a benchmark across model variants and sequence lengths. If your P95 target can't be reached on hosted models, we recommend a Dedicated evaluation where we run on your expected QPS and report throughput/latency and cost.
[05:15] Samir: Quick note on model variants — we offer Redwood-verified profiles and quantized variants that lower cost but may change quality slightly. We can help you pick.
[05:26] Maya: Any plug-and-play for analytics? We want per-route token and cost breakdowns in the console.
[05:33] Samir: Yep, Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and tracing. That's part of the hosted offering and included in Dedicated as well.
[05:42] Elena: About VPC — if we need peering for certain customer data flows, how long?
[05:48] Leah: VPC/private deployments require network setup and an SSO/KMS handshake — typically 3-6 weeks depending on legal and firewall rules.
[05:58] Ravi: Ok. For the first phase, let's do hosted pilot with credits then a technical deep dive to test Dedicated if needed. We want to ensure cost per inference at scale is viable.
[06:08] Samir: Sounds good. I'll send credits and the pricing spreadsheet. Leah will lead the benchmark deep dive.
[06:14] Maya: Great. One more question — do you have any out-of-the-box QA or eval tooling for prompt regressions?
[06:21] Leah: We do. Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks, regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll share the eval playbook.
[06:30] Jon: Any limitations on rate limits during a trial?
[06:34] Samir: We set generous trial quotas but caps depend on abuse prevention; for benchmark runs we can temporarily raise them with a heads-up.
[06:42] [cross-talk] Elena: — and SOC2 report access for procurement?
[06:45] Samir: Yes, procurement can get SOC2 docs under NDA; we'll include that in the folder.
[06:52] Maya: Who's the main contact at Redwood for billing/credits?
[06:55] Samir: Me for commercial — samir@redwood.ai. Leah will be technical.
[07:02] Ravi: Timeline recap: we need a demo for leadership in 3 weeks, pilot test results in ~6 weeks.
[07:10] Samir: We'll align on milestones.
[07:16] [20:00 - mid call technical dive snippet]
[20:00] Leah: For benchmarks we usually run three model sizes, vary sequence lengths (128, 512, 1024), and measure P50/P95/P99. We'll produce a spreadsheet with latency, throughput, and per-token cost.
[20:20] Jon: For our use case most prompts average 220 tokens and are single-turn. Peak QPS expected ~30, but burst to 100.
[20:32] Leah: Ok bursts to 100 — caching will help but Dedicated with autoscaling policies is ideal for predictable throughput.
[20:40] Samir: I'll note that down.
[35:00] Samir: Wrapping up — recap of action items and owners.
[35:12] Ravi: Sounds good.
[35:20] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll share the folder (pricing sheet, security whitepaper, eval runbook) and schedule the bench deep dive.
[35:30] Maya: Thanks.
[35:34] Elena: Thanks, bye.

End of meeting.
